Genomic Prediction via Integrated Modelling

Source: R/gpAim.R
gpAim.Rd

Fits a genomic best linear unbiased prediction (G-BLUP) model and extracts genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs) for all genotyped lines. Two computational paths are used depending on the relationship between the number of markers and lines:

vm path (markers > lines)

Constructs the genomic relationship matrix \(G = XX'/s\) (where \(X\) is the marker matrix and \(s\) is a scaling constant) and fits vm(line, G) as the genetic random effect in ASReml. GEBVs are the predicted values of this random effect, obtained via predict.asreml.

mbf path (lines \(\ge\) markers)

Models marker effects \(\mathbf{q}\) directly as i.i.d. random effects via ASReml's mbf() facility. GEBVs are then computed as \(\hat{\mathbf{g}} = M\hat{\mathbf{q}}\), where \(M\) is the \((\text{lines} \times \text{markers})\) genotype matrix and \(\hat{\mathbf{q}}\) are the marker effect BLUPs. This avoids the singularity of \(G\) when lines equal or exceed markers.

Usage

gpAim(baseModel, ...)

# Default S3 method
gpAim(baseModel, ...)

# S3 method for class 'asreml'
gpAim(
  baseModel,
  genObj,
  merge.by = NULL,
  fix.lines = TRUE,
  gen.type = "marker",
  force = FALSE,
  trace = TRUE,
  Trait = NULL,
  str = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

baseModel

A converged asreml model object representing the null model without any genomic genetic term. Should capture experimental design effects, spatial terms, and fixed covariates. The genetic line term should be included in the random formula; it is removed internally and replaced by the genomic term. If the model has not converged, one update attempt is made automatically.

...

Additional arguments passed to update.asreml, such as na.action = na.method(x = "include").

genObj

A genotypic data object of class "wgCross" (from primeCross, for biparental populations) or class "wgPanel" (from primePanel, for diversity panels). Must contain per-chromosome genotype matrices accessible at $geno[[chr]]$imputed.data (marker mode) or $geno[[chr]]$interval.data (interval mode).

merge.by

Character string naming the column present in both the phenotypic data and genObj linking lines across datasets.

fix.lines

Logical. If TRUE (default), lines in the phenotypic data that are absent from genObj are accommodated by adding a fixed Gomit factor and restricting the genomic random effect to genotyped lines only. See qtlAim for full details.

gen.type

Character string, either "marker" (default) or "interval". Determines which genotype scores are used to build the marker matrix \(M\). "marker" uses imputed marker scores ($imputed.data); "interval" uses interval midpoint scores ($interval.data) and requires a "wgCross" class genObj. For diversity panels ("wgPanel" class), gen.type = "marker" is required.

force

Logical. If FALSE (default), the vm path is used when markers exceed lines and the mbf path otherwise (automatic selection). Set force = TRUE to always use the mbf path regardless of the markers-to-lines ratio. The two paths are statistically equivalent.

trace

Logical or character string. If TRUE (default), ASReml output is printed to the console. If a file path character string, output is redirected there.

Trait

Character string naming a factor column in the phenotypic data identifying the environment or trial (e.g. "Trial"). When supplied, a multivariate G-BLUP model is fitted and per-environment GEBVs are returned. See str for how the variance structure of the additive genomic term is controlled. Default NULL (univariate).

str

Character string controlling the variance structure applied to the additive genomic term (vm() or mbf()) when Trait is non-NULL. Options:

NULL (default)

Mirror the structure on the genetic line term in baseModel's random formula: corh/corgh/ us maps to corgh(Trait):vm(); fa(Trait,k) maps to fa(Trait,k):vm(); diag stays as diag(Trait):vm() (independent per-environment GEBVs).

"corh" / "corgh" / "us"

Force corgh(Trait):vm(): heterogeneous variances with a common genetic correlation across environments.

"fa1", "fa2", ...

Force fa(Trait,k):vm() with \(k\) factors. The number must be explicit; str = "fa" alone returns an error.

"diag"

Force diag(Trait):vm(): independent per-environment GEBVs, no borrowing of information across environments.

Ignored when Trait = NULL. When str is supplied, the structure on the residual genetic term in baseModel is retained unchanged; only the additive genomic term is overridden.

Value

An object of class c("gpAim","asreml") – the fitted ASReml model augmented with a $GP list containing:

$gebv

A data.frame with columns for the line identifier, GEBV (genomic estimated breeding value), and SE (standard error of the GEBV).

$gen.type

The genotype data type used ("marker" or "interval").

$path

The computational path used ("vm" or "mbf").

$var.genetic

Estimated additive genetic variance \(V_g\).

$var.resid

Estimated residual variance \(V_e\).

$heritability

Estimated narrow-sense heritability \(h^2 = V_g/(V_g + V_e)\).

$n.markers

Number of markers used.

$rel.matrix

The genomic relationship matrix \(G\), stored for use in plot.gpAim.

$genetic.term

The name of the genetic line identifier column (as named in the returned $gebv data frame).

Additionally, the (possibly modified) phenotypic data frame is assigned to <response>.data in the calling environment.

Details

GEBV standard errors under the mbf path: For the mbf path, GEBV standard errors are computed using a diagonal approximation: \(SE(\hat{g}_i) \approx \sqrt{M_i^2 \cdot PEV(\hat{q})}\), where \(M_i\) is row \(i\) of the marker matrix and \(PEV(\hat{q})\) is the vector of prediction error variances for the marker effects. This approximation treats marker effects as independent, ignoring their covariances, and may underestimate true standard errors somewhat.

Heritability: Narrow-sense heritability is estimated as \(h^2 = V_g / (V_g + V_e)\), where \(V_g\) is the estimated additive genetic variance and \(V_e\) is the residual variance. For the vm path, \(V_g = \sigma^2 \cdot \lambda_{vm}\) where \(\lambda_{vm}\) is the vm variance parameter. For the mbf path, \(V_g = \sigma^2 \cdot \lambda_{mbf} \cdot \overline{\sum_j m_{ij}^2}\), where \(\overline{\sum_j m_{ij}^2}\) is the mean sum of squared marker scores per line.

Genomic relationship matrix: The relationship matrix \(G\) is stored in the returned object ($GP$rel.matrix) for both paths and is used by plot.gpAim to produce the relatedness heatmap. For the vm path this is the matrix used in model fitting; for the mbf path it is computed as \(MM'/s\) from the fitted marker matrix.

See also

print.gpAim, summary.gpAim, plot.gpAim, primePanel, primeCross, qtlAim, gwasAim

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(asreml)

# --- Diversity panel (vm path, markers > lines) ---
panel <- primePanel(geno = geno.mat, map = map.df, encoding = "012")
panel$pheno$line <- factor(line.ids)
base.mod <- asreml(yield ~ rep, random = ~ line, data = pheno.df)

gp.fit <- gpAim(base.mod, genObj = panel, merge.by = "line",
                trace = "trace.txt",
                na.action = na.method(x = "include"))

print(gp.fit)
summary(gp.fit)
plot(gp.fit, type = "caterpillar")
plot(gp.fit, type = "heatmap")
plot(gp.fit, type = "density", prop.select = 0.10)

# --- Biparental population (interval mode) ---
data(genoRxK, package = "wgAim")
genoRxK <- primeCross(genoRxK, impute = "Martinez", id = "Genotype")
base.mod2 <- asreml(yld ~ Type, random = ~ Genotype, data = phenoRxK)

gp.fit2 <- gpAim(base.mod2, genObj = genoRxK,
                 merge.by = "Genotype", gen.type = "interval")
} # }
